ligand-controlled regiodivergent hydroarylation of unactivated
allenes using DIBAL-H and aryl bromides. This approach
enables the selective synthesis of otherwise inaccessible α- and
γ-arylated alkenes from a common allene substrate. The
regioselectivity is precisely dictated by the phosphine ligand in
the Pd-catalyzed step, allowing mild, broad-scope reactions
with excellent regio- and stereocontrol. The same strategy is

high selectivity, and the synthetic versatility of the products
was showcased via Diels−Alder/oxidative aromatization
sequences. This study establishes a new ligand-directed
platform for achieving regiodivergent C−C bond formation
from allenes beyond the reach of conventional hydroarylation
chemistry.
